title: smart-routing-fallback-debug-scratchpad-alex
content:
Context:
Quick personal notes while triaging the 2026-02-28 regional failover that caused elevated 503 rates for outbound requests routed to eu-west-1. Scope: smart-routing + fallback policies + cross-region DNS routing.

Timeline (condensed):
- 2026-02-28 09:12 UTC: Pager alert - 503 spike seen by synthetic pings (eu-west-1).
- 09:15 UTC: Confirmed increased error rate for requests pinned to model: gpt-large-v2 (eu variants).
- 09:18 UTC: Failover policy kicked but some requests stayed in-flight and returned 503s.
- 09:42 UTC: Rollback of recent routing change reduced error rate.

Commands I ran (repro/inspection):
- kubectl get pods -n routing --selector=app=smart-router -o wide
  -> saw 2/5 pods in CrashLoopBackOff on eu-west-1 cluster (OOMKilled).

- kubectl logs smart-router-3 -n routing --since=1h | grep -i fallback
  -> repeated: "fallback evaluation failed: policy mismatch for model_variant" + stack traces for policy-evaluator.go:127

- curl -v 'https://api.redwood.test/generate' -H 'X-Region-Hint: eu' -d '{"model":"gpt-large-v2"}'
  -> intermittent 503, response body: "service unavailable: no healthy endpoints for routing-key"

- checked envoy metrics: /stats for smart-router -> saw high upstream_rq_5xx ratio for upstream cluster 'model-eu-west-a'

Relevant log snippets:
- 2026-02-28T09:16:32Z [policy-evaluator] ERROR fallback evaluation failed: requested variant 'q4f' not allowed for customer-tier 'free' (policy id=fallback-eu-2026-02-28)
- 2026-02-28T09:16:33Z [router] WARN unable to select fallback: no compatible variant found for model=gpt-large-v2 req_id=trace-0a8f
- 2026-02-28T09:18:41Z [envoy] upstream_reset: connection failure, errno=111, details='connection refused'

Hypotheses:
1) Recent policy change (fallback-eu-2026-02-28) added stricter variant compatibility rules (disallowed q4f for free tier). This reduced available fallbacks; combined with OOMKilled router pods caused inability to route and several requests had no fallback -> 503s.
2) Autoscaler on eu-west-1 didn't spin up compatible capacity quickly because fallback routing constrained to specific sub-pools (tagged 'low-latency'), causing temporary blackholing.
3) There's a bug in policy-evaluator where when primary route is unhealthy it doesn't re-evaluate globally-scoped fallback list (only local), so cross-region fallback wasn't considered.

Config excerpts I inspected (original saved in /tmp):
- fallback policy (human-readable):
  id: fallback-eu-2026-02-28
  allow_variants: [q8_0, q4f]
  disallow_for_tiers: {free: [q4f]}
  prefer_regions: [eu, us]
- router pool tags: low-latency, batch-enabled, q4-capable

Quick repro idea:
- Simulate a router pod OOM (scale down to 2/5) and send synthetic traffic pinned to eu-west-1 while enforcing policy that disallows q4f for free tier -> expect to reproduce 503s when remaining routers can't find compatible fallbacks.

Immediate mitigation applied:
- 09:30 UTC: Reverted fallback-eu-2026-02-28 policy to previous (fallback-eu-2026-01) which allowed q4f for free tier.
- 09:35 UTC: Increased HPA minReplicas for smart-router in eu-west-1 from 3 -> 5.
- 09:47 UTC: Error rates returned near baseline.

Open questions / next steps:
- Why did policy-evaluator return "no compatible variant" even when q8_0 was allowed? (need full decision trace logs)
- Add end-to-end eval to assert that when primary is unhealthy, global fallback list is considered (tests missing).
- Instrument policy-evaluator to dump the candidate list when fallback selection fails (trace-level).
- Run chaos test: scale router pods down and validate synthetic traffic still finds cross-region fallback.

TODOs (personal):
- [ ] Pull decision trace logs from 09:15-09:20 from logging-archive (Ethan has access).
- [ ] File a bug with policy-evaluator team (assign to @Taylor) with decision traces attached.
- [ ] Add unit test for multi-region fallback scenario in routing service (PR link in linked_artifacts).
- [ ] Draft a short postmortem skeleton for ops-review.

Notes to self: keep this doc rough — copy to Confluence after triage when we have decision traces.

Trace IDs seen: trace-0a8f, trace-14b2, trace-1c99 (save them for log searches).

-- Alex
